ppaDeals.note: First nuclear restart in the database and the most famous power deal in the market. RESTART, distinct from Clinton (relicensing). Grid PPA not colocation: Constellation explicit that no Microsoft data center sits at the plant; power matched to PJM load on an accounting basis. Capex per kW (~$1,916) is a striking contrast to campus capex ($10,000+/kW) and gas generation ($3,000/kW): nuclear restart is the cheapest firm carbon free MW in the book. Verified from Constellation 10-Q and IR release.

ppaDeals.name: Susquehanna PPA (AWS)
ppaDeals.structure: Front of the meter (RESTRUCTURED from colocated behind the meter after FERC rejection)
ppaDeals.capexFlag: not disclosed; $18B is notional revenue over 17 yr contract per Talen investor presentation, not capex
ppaDeals.creditSupport: Amazon offtake (investment grade); Talen acts as retail supplier
ppaDeals.location: Susquehanna nuclear plant, Salem Township, PA (2.5 GW, 2 units)
ppaDeals.status: Amended PPA Jun 11 2025; ramps 840-1,200 MW by 2029, 1,680-1,920 MW by 2032; FTM transition spring 2026

provenance.disclosed: up to 1,920 MW, ~$18B notional revenue (Talen investor deck), 17 yr through 2042, ramp schedule, FTM restructuring, Talen as retail supplier, PPL delivers, FERC rejected BTM ISA Nov 2024 and Apr 2025

ppaDeals.note: THE regulatory case study in the database. Originally colocated behind the meter; FERC rejected the amended interconnection agreement (Nov 2024, reaffirmed Apr 2025), forcing a restructure to front of the meter (Jun 2025) where Susquehanna injects into PJM, Talen is retail supplier, PPL delivers, and no FERC approval is needed. Proves the colocated/BTM vs grid/FTM topology distinction in the PPA tab is not academic: regulation forced an $18B deal to change its physical structure. 300 MW BTM remains interim until transmission reconfig spring 2026. Also includes SMR exploration. Verified from Talen 8-K, 10-K, and IR release.

ppaDeals.type: Nuclear SMR option / master development agreement
ppaDeals.structure: Master Plant Development Agreement + PPAs per plant; log as OPTION not firm procurement
ppaDeals.capexFlag: not disclosed; SMR fleet development cost not stated
ppaDeals.creditSupport: Google demand signal / PPAs per plant; early stage
ppaDeals.location: First plant Hermes 2, Oak Ridge, TN
ppaDeals.status: MPDA signed Oct 14 2024; first firm PPA (via TVA, up to 50 MW) Aug 2025; fleet up to 500 MW by 2035

provenance.disclosed: Master Plant Development Agreement, up to 500 MWe by 2035, first plant Hermes 2 by 2030, world's first corporate multi deployment SMR agreement, Aug 2025 TVA PPA for up to 50 MW to Google TN/AL data centers
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: contracted (50 MW) is 10% of aspiration (500 MW)
provenance.notDisclosed: price, total value, per plant terms, full fleet timing

ppaDeals.note: LOG AS OPTION, NOT PROCUREMENT. Critical announced vs contracted gap: the headline 500 MW by 2035 is a development pathway (a fleet of SMRs that do not yet exist), while the only FIRM contracted power is up to 50 MW from Hermes 2 via a TVA PPA (Aug 2025). Anyone logging 500 MW as procured power is wrong: it is an option on a fleet, priced as a demand signal to fund development. SMR technology risk, licensing risk, and first of a kind construction risk all sit ahead of it. Verified from Google blog, Kairos release, and World Nuclear News.

financingDeals.name: Hyperion JV
financingDeals.capitalPartners: Blue Owl funds 80% (~$7B cash), PIMCO (~$18B debt anchor), BlackRock ($3B, bond investor not equity partner), Morgan Stanley (arranger); issuer Beignet Investor LLC
financingDeals.structure: Development JV via bankruptcy remote SPV; BlackRock is a bondholder, Blue Owl is the 80% equity; Meta contributes land and CIP and takes a ~$3B one time distribution to align to 80/20; operating lease back to Meta (4 yr initial term, extension options) + 16 yr capped residual value guarantee; A+ rated 144A for life bonds
financingDeals.leverage: reported figures vary; do not impute a clean ratio without the OM (Blue Owl ~$7B cash equity + Meta contributed basis against $27.294B notes)
financingDeals.creditSupport: Meta operating lease + 16 yr capped residual value guarantee (threshold not publicly quantified, unlike El Paso)
financingDeals.status: Notes priced Oct 16 2025; JV announced Oct 21 2025

provenance.disclosed: 80/20 Blue Owl / Meta split, ~$27B total dev cost, Blue Owl ~$7B cash, Meta ~$3B one time distribution, Meta contributed land and CIP, 4 yr lease + extensions, 16 yr RVG, $27.294B Beignet notes at 6.581% due May 30 2049, T+225, A+ S&P single agency, 144A for life
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: capex ~$13,500 per kW (imputed from reported $27B / 2 GW)
provenance.analystImputed: equity cushion reported inconsistently across outlets; the 90% leverage figure previously carried does not reconcile and was removed
provenance.notDisclosed: RVG threshold amount and step down, rent per MW year, precise equity vs debt split reconciliation, guarantee triggers and caps

financingDeals.note: First disclosed instance of Meta's off balance sheet JV template, refined at El Paso Jul 2026. Beignet Investor LLC is the bankruptcy remote issuer; naming it signals filing level reading. BlackRock appears as a $3B bond investor, NOT the equity partner (that is Blue Owl) and NOT to be confused with the separate Meta / BlackRock El Paso JV. Auction ran Apollo + KKR vs PIMCO + Blue Owl; 144A won for syndication. Corrected Aug 2026: debt was carried at $26B, actual $27.294B; 90% leverage note removed as unreconciled.

financingDeals.name: El Paso campus JV
financingDeals.tenant: Meta (20% JV owner, lessee, initial sole occupant, operator)
financingDeals.capitalPartners: BlackRock funds 80% (~$4.9B cash), GIP and HPS (BlackRock infrastructure and private credit arms); $12.5B debt financing funds part of BlackRock's contribution
financingDeals.structure: Development JV; BlackRock 80% / Meta 20%; ~$14B total development cost funded pro rata; Meta contributes land and CIP (~$2.3B) and takes a ~$1B one time distribution to align to 80/20; operating lease back to Meta (4 yr initial term, four extension options, ~20 yr potential) + 16 yr residual value guarantee
financingDeals.capexFlag: computed: ~$14B total development cost / 1 GW = ~$14,000 per kW (includes power, cooling, connectivity per release)
financingDeals.creditSupport: Meta operating lease + residual value guarantee, aggregate threshold ~$13B decreasing over time; within first 16 yrs Meta pays shortfall between fair value and the RVG threshold for covered property
financingDeals.status: Announced Jul 28 2026; expected to close within days; capacity online from 2028

provenance.disclosed: 80/20 split, ~$14B total dev cost, Meta land and CIP ~$2.3B, BlackRock cash ~$4.9B, Meta $1B one time distribution, $12.5B debt financing, 1 GW capacity, online 2028, 4 yr lease with four extensions across ~20 yr, RVG threshold ~$13B decreasing, 16 yr RVG window, Meta >$10B site investment figure, Morgan Stanley and JP Morgan advised Meta
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: equity ~$7.2B (2.3 contributed + 4.9 cash); capex ~$14,000 per kW; RVG threshold ~93% of total dev cost at inception
provenance.notDisclosed: rent per MW year, debt terms and rating, RVG step down schedule, whether debt sits at JV or a Beignet style issuer, refinancing plan

financingDeals.note: Second disclosed instance of Meta's off balance sheet JV template after Hyperion: identical 80/20, four year lease inside a 20 year envelope, 16 yr RVG, contributed land plus CIP, one time true up distribution. El Paso is the cleaner data point because the RVG threshold is quantified (~$13B, decreasing) where Hyperion's was not. Meta has effectively productized this structure. Advisors overlap with Hyperion (Morgan Stanley, Kirkland for the capital partner). Watch: whether the $12.5B debt terms out into a Beignet style 144A issue, giving a third notching data point alongside Hyperion and the Nexus bridge.

financingDeals.name: Nexus Hubbard campus financing
financingDeals.parties: Nexus Data Centers / Anthropic / Google / Morgan Stanley led bank consortium
financingDeals.announced: Jul 2026 (reported; could be announced as soon as Thursday)
financingDeals.capitalPartners: Morgan Stanley (lead arranger, bank consortium), Evercore (sole financial advisor to Nexus), Google (guarantor and ~20% equity), Broadcom (separate vendor financing for TPUs)
financingDeals.structure: SPV project financing: $14B bridge loan plus revolving credit facility. Behind the meter 1.6 GW natural gas plant integrated with campus. Google guarantees Anthropic lease and power payment obligations across 4 leases and their PPAs; Google receives ~20% equity in the data center and power project. Chips financed separately by Broadcom vendor financing.
financingDeals.capexFlag: not disclosed: total project cost not stated, so capex per kW cannot be computed. $15B is debt quantum only, not total cost.
financingDeals.creditSupport: Google guarantee of lease and power payment obligations, sized to the minimum the banks required. Google accounts for backstops as credit derivatives. On tenant default Google may assume the leases and self use or sublease, or terminate the backstop obligation by paying a fee.
financingDeals.powerSource: Behind the meter natural gas, 1.6 GW, sited for proximity to major gas pipelines, expressly to avoid utility interconnection queue. Campus could grow past 1.6 GW.
financingDeals.chips: Google TPUs, codesigned with Broadcom, financed via separate Broadcom vendor financing deal with Anthropic
financingDeals.status: Advanced talks reported; construction began early 2025
financingDeals.sponsorBackground: Nexus founded by energy industry veterans from large scale natural gas projects. CEO Ivan Van der Walt formerly of NextDecade (LNG export developer); NextDecade former CFO also joined.

provenance.disclosed: debt quantum $15B, bridge $14B plus revolver, 1.6 GW BTM gas, ~20% Google equity, 4 leases plus PPAs guaranteed, Morgan Stanley lead, Evercore advisor, Broadcom vendor financing, construction start early 2025, Alphabet credit derivative max exposure $43.8B as of Jun 30 2026
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: none yet; total project cost undisclosed
provenance.analystImputed: expectation that the bridge is refinanced into permanent capital (bonds or ABS) within 12 to 24 months, based on bridge structure and phase convention
provenance.notDisclosed: total project cost, guarantee cap amount, backstop termination fee, Broadcom financing terms, lease term years, rent per MW year, Anthropic lease start dates

financingDeals.note: Third Google backstop where Anthropic is ultimate customer, after TeraWulf and Hut8. Pattern: credit support compensated with ~20% equity or equity linked position rather than a fee, matching Hyperion 80/20 and Equinix xScale 80/20. Guarantee is optionality not charity: Google can step into contracted capacity on default. Vendor financing circularity: the chip supplier guarantees the project that buys its chips. Comparable: Nvidia in talks on a reported $250B backstop for an OpenAI Ohio campus up to 10 GW. Anthropic has signed 12+ preliminary leases targeting 10+ GW, leasing led by Tim Hughes, formerly of Stack Infrastructure.
financingDeals.watchItems: 1) Alphabet credit derivative maximum potential exposure line, quarter over quarter, as the aggregate thesis metric. 2) The bridge take out: size, format, and whether it prices off Google support rather than Nexus credit, giving a second Hyperion style notching data point. 3) Whether gas pipeline capacity becomes the new binding queue, replacing transmission.

financingDeals.name: SB Energy Ohio campus (Nvidia backstop)
financingDeals.parties: SB Energy (SoftBank) / OpenAI / Nvidia / US Department of Commerce / Government of Japan
financingDeals.announced: Jul 2026 (WSJ reported Aug 2026; in talks, terms not finalized)
financingDeals.tenant: OpenAI (advanced talks to lease; would be OpenAI's first project as direct tenant). Anthropic, Microsoft and Google also spoke to Commerce about the site.
financingDeals.capitalPartners: Nvidia (guarantor of a series of financing vehicles, ~$250B; separately has invested $30B in OpenAI and is discussing financing chip purchases of up to ~$350B), Government of Japan ($33B into the power project under a tariff trade deal), SoftBank (SB Energy owner and major OpenAI investor), US federal government (land and power allocation)
financingDeals.structure: Nvidia guarantees a series of financing vehicles covering the data center lease and the buildout debt, expressly NOT the chips. Chips financed separately in a parallel Nvidia arrangement. Power project funded by Japan at $33B on federal land, operated by SB Energy for a fee paid by the US government. Power sales revenue split between Japan and the US until Japan recoups its $33B, after which the US government receives 90% of revenue.
financingDeals.capexFlag: not computable: the >$500B figure explicitly includes chips, so it cannot be divided by capacity to produce a facility capex per kW comparable to other records.
financingDeals.creditSupport: Nvidia guarantee of roughly $250B across financing vehicles, covering lease and buildout debt but not chips. Rationale as reported: OpenAI has no investment grade credit rating as an unprofitable private company, so the guarantee lets the developer raise debt on better terms than OpenAI could alone.
financingDeals.powerSource: Natural gas power project on federal land, funded by Japan, operated by SB Energy. Power allocation controlled by the US government with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick involved in deciding who receives it.
financingDeals.location: Southern Ohio, decommissioned uranium enrichment site roughly 50 miles south of Columbus (federal land)
financingDeals.status: In talks; groundbreaking held March 2026 with Lutnick, Son and Energy Secretary Chris Wright. First phase expected 2028 at roughly 800 MW.

provenance.disclosed: VERIFIED WSJ Aug 2026: ~$250B Nvidia guarantee, 10 GW capacity, >$500B total including chips, $33B Japanese investment, revenue split terms, 90% US share post recoupment, first phase 2028 at ~800MW, federal land siting, Nvidia $30B invested in OpenAI, ~$350B potential chip financing, OpenAI compute spend projection raised to ~$750B through 2030 from ~$600B, Nvidia ~$5T market value, Nvidia annual report risk disclosure on customer credit exposure
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: first phase is 8% of ultimate capacity (800MW of 10GW); guarantee is roughly half of stated total project cost
provenance.analystImputed: the Japan recoupment then 90/10 split is structurally a preferred return followed by a sponsor promote, applied to a sovereign rather than a fund
provenance.notDisclosed: lease term, rent per MW year, the identity and structure of the financing vehicles, guarantee triggers and caps, chip financing terms, what SB Energy's operating fee is

financingDeals.note: INDUSTRY TERM CAPTURED: the arrangement is described within the industry as a credit wrapper, where investment grade technology companies use their balance sheets to help smaller companies borrow for infrastructure. Same family as Google backstopping Anthropic at TeraWulf, Hut8, and Nexus Hubbard, described as partly intended to increase sales of Google's own TPUs. Federal land is being used expressly to avoid the permitting and local opposition snarling projects elsewhere. Nvidia's own annual report warns that data center funding arrangements could lower near term cash flows and increase exposure to customer credit risk, so the guarantor has disclosed the risk it is taking. SOURCE UPGRADE: verified against WSJ ('Nvidia in Talks With OpenAI to Guarantee $250 Billion Financing'), Aug 2026. WSJ confirms $250B guarantee covers lease and buildout debt but NOT chips; separate ~$350B chip financing and $30B Nvidia equity in OpenAI are distinct arrangements. Would be OpenAI's first data center as a tenant. Status remains in talks: terms not finalized, deal could fall apart.
financingDeals.watchItems: 1) Whether the deal closes at all, since terms are not finalized. 2) The three layer circularity: Nvidia equity in OpenAI, Nvidia guarantee of OpenAI's lease, Nvidia financing of OpenAI's chip purchases. 3) Government allocated power as a new siting channel: who else receives allocations and on what basis. 4) Whether federal land siting becomes a repeatable permitting bypass.

financingDeals.name: CoreWeave / Meta compute agreement
financingDeals.structure: Take or pay dedicated GPU cloud capacity; multi site; early NVIDIA Vera Rubin; inference focused. Meta pays for guaranteed access regardless of usage.
financingDeals.creditSupport: None; rests directly on Meta investment grade credit (no third party guarantee)
financingDeals.financingNote: CoreWeave raised ~$4.25B around the deal: $3B convertibles + $1.25B high yield

provenance.disclosed: $21B expansion through Dec 2032, prior $14.2B (Sep 2025), ~$35B combined, Vera Rubin, inference focus, CoreWeave $4.25B debt raise, 2025 rev $5.13B (+168%), backlog >$66B
provenance.analystImputed: take or pay inferred from reporting
provenance.notDisclosed: MW capacity, price per GPU hr, sites, take or pay floor

financingDeals.note: The neocloud archetype the curriculum is built around, finally logged. Meta is CoreWeave's largest commercial relationship. UNLIKE Fluidstack/Nexus there is NO third party credit wrapper: CoreWeave lends against Meta's own investment grade credit directly, which is why it is financeable without a guarantor. Concentration arc = thesis in motion: Microsoft was 62% of CoreWeave 2024 revenue (S-1); now no single customer >35% after Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic. Verified from CoreWeave IR release and CNBC.

financingDeals.parties: Brookfield / NextEra / US Department of Energy
financingDeals.tenant: Not disclosed; Brookfield develops and operates the campus, tenant(s) TBD

thesis.argument: Model weights are becoming free; megawatts are not. As open weight models commoditize the middle of the stack, durable value migrates to the physical layer: chips, buildings, power, and interconnection. The structures in this deck are the best informed players locking up decades of that layer. Capital structure determines when and how you suffer if wrong, not whether.
